items.title: Tim Ries interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 19, 2022
items.q: I played the melody and then Mike played an alto solo and it was like I didn’t need to solo.

ctx.x: You know I loved the moment — audience members sometimes don’t know these kind of little things that go on, but I think it was in “Willow Weep for Me” and the form had gone to its conclusion, I think it was an alto solo and I saw you like four beats before you stood up and you said something to Ron and the band went to the bridge instead of back to the top. So I’m pretty sure you said, “Bridge.” And that’s so, I love the onstage etiquette and the learning of the craft and how things work. I don’t have a question…

No it’s one of those things because like I played the melody and then Mike played an alto solo and it was like I didn’t need to solo. It was like the song was long enough. I was okay with just playing the melody and then Mike took the solos like hey let’s take the bridge out, we don’t need more than that. And yeah so that’s like, you know, why make a tune ten minutes when it could be — say as much as you need in five.

Well I’m pretty sure you made musical history last night because I’m going to guess that there’s never been a medley of “Willow Weep for Me” into “I Can’t Get No Satisfaction” into the “Beer Barrel Polka.” So congratulations.
